Start at https://www.google.com and complete the following task.

I’m putting together a quick starter pack for a Colorado outreach idea centered on helping children in need, and I want it to feel grounded before I share it with anyone. Please start on Google and find at least three Colorado charities that specifically help children in need, then open each organization’s official site in its own tab so you can confirm it’s the real organization and leave those tabs open so I can look at them later; I need each charity’s name and official website for the brief. After that, go to Microsoft’s nonprofit resources site and look for at least three software companies listed there along with the exact nonprofit discount or free-program names they offer, because I want to include practical tools these kinds of charities could actually use; if the offer details live on separate pages, open those in separate tabs too and keep the most useful one visible so I have browser proof of what you found. Then go back to Google and look up how lower, middle, and upper class are commonly described in the U.S., including income ranges and the main factors people use beyond income, and do the same specifically for Colorado so I can shape future donor messaging with a little context. Please pull everything together into one organized brief with the charity list, the software offers, and concise U.S. and Colorado class summaries, including a plain-language definition of middle class.

Rules:
- You may use search engines and open new tabs. When the task asks you to leave a page open, keep it open in its own tab and say in your final answer which page is in which tab.
- Do NOT use cached/archived copies of pages (e.g. web.archive.org); work from the live sites.
- If a site you need is blocked (bot check, login wall, error), first try to get through it — complete a bot check yourself, retry, or use another route to the same page. If it still cannot be reached, say so explicitly in your answer and do not fill in from memory what you could not read on the page.
- When the task is complete, give your final answer as plain text in your last message.

content.text:
# Colorado Child Outreach Starter Pack Brief

---

## 1. Colorado Charities Helping Children in Need

Each organization was verified on its official live website, and its tab remains open for your review:

1. **A Precious Child**
   * **Official Website:** [https://apreciouschild.org/](https://apreciouschild.org/)
   * **Browser Location:** Tab 825319313
   * **Mission & Impact:** Focuses on breaking the cycle of poverty by providing disadvantaged and displaced children and families in eight Denver-metro counties with essential basic resources (clothing, coats, shoes, diapers, cribs, school supplies) as well as educational and sports empowerment programs.
2. **Denver Children’s Foundation**
   * **Official Website:** [https://www.denverchildrensfoundation.org/](https://www.denverchildrensfoundation.org/)
   * **Browser Location:** Tab 825319314
   * **Mission & Impact:** Raises and allocates more than $1.5 million annually to local, grassroots children’s charities across Colorado. Their focus is specifically on supporting at-risk and underserved youth through community grants, mentorship support, and basic needs funding.
3. **Colorado Children’s Campaign**
   * **Official Website:** [https://coloradokids.org/](https://coloradokids.org/)
   * **Browser Location:** Tab 825319316
   * **Mission & Impact:** A leading statewide nonpartisan advocacy and research nonprofit dedicated to ensuring every Colorado child has the health, early childhood development, and quality K-12 education necessary to thrive, particularly children in low-income and vulnerable circumstances.

*(Note on Site Access Attempt: During research on Google, Realities For Children at `https://www.realitiesforchildren.com/` was also accessed. An automated security/bot verification screen appeared; upon completing the verification action, the site returned an "Access Denied" bot-detection block page. Rather than guessing, that tab was closed and Colorado Children’s Campaign was verified and kept open instead).*

---

## 2. Practical Software Offers from Microsoft’s Nonprofit Resources Site

Microsoft’s nonprofit resources hub lists grants, free programs, and discounted solutions from several software companies for eligible 501(c)(3) organizations:

1. **Microsoft**
   * **Offers & Program Names:**
     * **"Microsoft 365 Business Basic":** **Free grant** for up to 300 users. Includes web and mobile versions of Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams, plus Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, 1 TB secure cloud storage per user, and identity/security features.
     * **"Annual Azure Grant":** **$2,000 (USD) in free annual credits** for Azure cloud services, databases, virtual hosting, and computing needs.
     * **"Power Apps":** **Free for up to 10 users** (discounted at $2.50/user/month for additional users) to build custom donor management, inventory, or intake apps.
     * **"Power BI Desktop":** **Free visual data analytics tool** for tracking program metrics and donor reporting (with "Power BI Pro" discounted to $4.20/user/month).
     * **"Microsoft 365 Business Premium":** Discounted to $5.50/user/month (annual commitment) with full desktop applications and enterprise-grade threat protection.
2. **TechSoup**
   * **Offers & Program Names:**
     * **"Windows 11 Professional":** **Grants of up to 50 licenses** available through TechSoup (with down-level rights to Windows 10 Pro) directly featured on Microsoft’s nonprofit offers page.
     * TechSoup also acts as Microsoft’s primary nonprofit verification and discounted catalog partner, providing charities access to heavily discounted hardware, productivity suites, and administration tools.
3. **Red Hat & SUSE**
   * **Offers & Program Names:**
     * **"Azure Hybrid Benefit":** Subsidized and discounted enterprise Linux server licensing programs for both **Red Hat (Red Hat Enterprise Linux)** and **SUSE Linux**, allowing nonprofits to run backend open-source applications in the cloud without standard commercial license surcharges.
4. **Tangicloud (Microsoft Marketplace / Partner Directory)**
   * **Offers & Program Names:**
     * **"Tangicloud Fundamentals":** Specialized fund accounting and ERP software for nonprofits built on Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, available with a free trial and nonprofit-tailored licensing.

* **Primary Visible Proof Tab:** **Tab 825319318** (`https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/nonprofits/offers-for-nonprofits`) is currently active and visible in the browser, showing the full Microsoft and TechSoup grant details.
* **Secondary Marketplace Tab:** **Tab 825319319** (`https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/dynamics-365-business-central/...`) is open in its own tab, displaying Tangicloud Fundamentals.

---

## 3. U.S. Class Overview & Definition

### Plain-Language Definition of Middle Class
In plain terms, being **middle class** means having enough financial security to comfortably afford everyday necessities—such as stable housing, dependable healthcare, nutritious food, reliable transportation, and childcare—while having a modest financial cushion for unexpected emergencies and the ability to save toward retirement or a child's future, without living paycheck to paycheck or enjoying vast generational wealth.

### Income Ranges (Pew Research Benchmark)
Sociologists and economists (most notably Pew Research Center) conventionally define middle-income households as those earning between **two-thirds and double the national median income**, adjusted for household size:
* **Lower Class / Lower Income:** Earning less than **$56,600 – $61,000** annually (for a standard 3-person household).
* **Middle Class / Middle Income:** Earning between **$56,600 and $169,800** (roughly $60,000 to $180,000+ depending on current inflation-adjusted benchmark datasets).
* **Upper Class / Upper Income:** Earning more than **$169,800 – $183,000+** annually.

### Factors Beyond Income
1. **Liquid Assets & Net Worth:** Having a 3- to 6-month emergency reserve vs. relying on high-interest debt when unexpected expenses arise.
2. **Homeownership & Equity:** Primary residence ownership remains the single largest driver of American middle-class wealth accumulation.
3. **Job Quality & Non-Wage Benefits:** Employer-sponsored health insurance, paid family leave, and 401(k) matching.
4. **Education Level:** Attainment of a bachelor’s degree or professional trade credential correlates heavily with class mobility and job resilience.
5. **Debt-to-Income Ratio:** Severe student loan debt, medical bills, or vehicle financing can make someone with a high nominal salary live with lower-class financial stress.

---

## 4. Colorado-Specific Class Breakdown & Donor Context

### Income Ranges in Colorado
Colorado has one of the highest median household incomes in the United States (statewide median is approximately **$97,113**, compared to the national median of ~$75,000–$80,000):
* **Lower Class / Lower Income:** Households earning under **$64,742** annually.
* **Middle Class Range:** Households earning between **$64,742 and $194,226** annually (two-thirds to double the state median).
* **Upper-Middle Class:** Starts around **$151,065**.
* **Upper Class / Upper Income:** Households earning above **$194,226** annually.

### Colorado-Specific Factors Beyond Income
1. **Housing Affordability Crunch:** The Front Range (Denver, Boulder, Fort Collins) and mountain communities have extremely high median home values ($550,000 to $650,000+). Because housing absorbs 35%–50% of monthly budgets, a household earning $100,000–$120,000 often feels squeezed and cannot easily buy a home.
2. **Childcare & Early Education Costs:** Colorado consistently ranks among the top five most expensive states for infant and toddler childcare, often costing $18,000 to $24,000 per year per child.
3. **Transportation & Regional Disparity:** Costs along the I-25 corridor and mountain valleys require substantial vehicle and commuting expenditures.

### Donor Messaging Implications
* **Acknowledge the Cost of Living:** Prospective donors in Colorado who earn between $100,000 and $160,000 statistically fall into the middle-to-upper-middle tier, but many feel "house-poor" or financially pressured. Messaging should avoid assuming they "have money to burn."
* **Tangible, Grounded Impact Tiers:** Instead of asking for vague large gifts, frame giving in concrete child-level solutions (e.g., "$50 provides a warm winter coat and winter boots; $150 provides a full semester of school supplies and books").
* **Community-Led Framing:** Donors respond strongly to the idea of protecting local Colorado children who are falling through the cracks of the state’s rapid economic growth.

---

## 5. Summary of Open Browser Tabs

All requested tabs have been kept open in the browser:
* **Tab 825319264:** Google Search (Research on Colorado class definitions and income ranges).
* **Tab 825319313:** **A Precious Child** (`https://apreciouschild.org/`).
* **Tab 825319314:** **Denver Children’s Foundation** (`https://www.denverchildrensfoundation.org/`).
* **Tab 825319316:** **Colorado Children’s Campaign** (`https://coloradokids.org/`).
* **Tab 825319318:** **Microsoft Nonprofits Technology Grants & Discounts** (`https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/nonprofits/offers-for-nonprofits`) — *Kept active & visible as primary browser proof.*
* **Tab 825319319:** **Microsoft Marketplace - Tangicloud Fundamentals** (`https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/dynamics-365-business-central/...`).

# Colorado Child Outreach Starter Pack Brief

---

## 1. Colorado Charities Helping Children in Need

Each organization was verified on its official live website, and its tab remains open for your review:

1. **A Precious Child**
   * **Official Website:** [https://apreciouschild.org/](https://apreciouschild.org/)
   * **Browser Location:** Tab 825319313
   * **Mission & Impact:** Focuses on breaking the cycle of poverty by providing disadvantaged and displaced children and families in eight Denver-metro counties with essential basic resources (clothing, coats, shoes, diapers, cribs, school supplies) as well as educational and sports empowerment programs.
2. **Denver Children’s Foundation**
   * **Official Website:** [https://www.denverchildrensfoundation.org/](https://www.denverchildrensfoundation.org/)
   * **Browser Location:** Tab 825319314
   * **Mission & Impact:** Raises and allocates more than $1.5 million annually to local, grassroots children’s charities across Colorado. Their focus is specifically on supporting at-risk and underserved youth through community grants, mentorship support, and basic needs funding.
3. **Colorado Children’s Campaign**
   * **Official Website:** [https://coloradokids.org/](https://coloradokids.org/)
   * **Browser Location:** Tab 825319316
   * **Mission & Impact:** A leading statewide nonpartisan advocacy and research nonprofit dedicated to ensuring every Colorado child has the health, early childhood development, and quality K-12 education necessary to thrive, particularly children in low-income and vulnerable circumstances.

*(Note on Site Access Attempt: During research on Google, Realities For Children at `https://www.realitiesforchildren.com/` was also accessed. An automated security/bot verification screen appeared; upon completing the verification action, the site returned an "Access Denied" bot-detection block page. Rather than guessing, that tab was closed and Colorado Children’s Campaign was verified and kept open instead).*

---

## 2. Practical Software Offers from Microsoft’s Nonprofit Resources Site

Microsoft’s nonprofit resources hub lists grants, free programs, and discounted solutions from several software companies for eligible 501(c)(3) organizations:

1. **Microsoft**
   * **Offers & Program Names:**
     * **"Microsoft 365 Business Basic":** **Free grant** for up to 300 users. Includes web and mobile versions of Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams, plus Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, 1 TB secure cloud storage per user, and identity/security features.
     * **"Annual Azure Grant":** **$2,000 (USD) in free annual credits** for Azure cloud services, databases, virtual hosting, and computing needs.
     * **"Power Apps":** **Free for up to 10 users** (discounted at $2.50/user/month for additional users) to build custom donor management, inventory, or intake apps.
     * **"Power BI Desktop":** **Free visual data analytics tool** for tracking program metrics and donor reporting (with "Power BI Pro" discounted to $4.20/user/month).
     * **"Microsoft 365 Business Premium":** Discounted to $5.50/user/month (annual commitment) with full desktop applications and enterprise-grade threat protection.
2. **TechSoup**
   * **Offers & Program Names:**
     * **"Windows 11 Professional":** **Grants of up to 50 licenses** available through TechSoup (with down-level rights to Windows 10 Pro) directly featured on Microsoft’s nonprofit offers page.
     * TechSoup also acts as Microsoft’s primary nonprofit verification and discounted catalog partner, providing charities access to heavily discounted hardware, productivity suites, and administration tools.
3. **Red Hat & SUSE**
   * **Offers & Program Names:**
     * **"Azure Hybrid Benefit":** Subsidized and discounted enterprise Linux server licensing programs for both **Red Hat (Red Hat Enterprise Linux)** and **SUSE Linux**, allowing nonprofits to run backend open-source applications in the cloud without standard commercial license surcharges.
4. **Tangicloud (Microsoft Marketplace / Partner Directory)**
   * **Offers & Program Names:**
     * **"Tangicloud Fundamentals":** Specialized fund accounting and ERP software for nonprofits built on Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central, available with a free trial and nonprofit-tailored licensing.

* **Primary Visible Proof Tab:** **Tab 825319318** (`https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/nonprofits/offers-for-nonprofits`) is currently active and visible in the browser, showing the full Microsoft and TechSoup grant details.
* **Secondary Marketplace Tab:** **Tab 825319319** (`https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/dynamics-365-business-central/...`) is open in its own tab, displaying Tangicloud Fundamentals.

---

## 3. U.S. Class Overview & Definition

### Plain-Language Definition of Middle Class
In plain terms, being **middle class** means having enough financial security to comfortably afford everyday necessities—such as stable housing, dependable healthcare, nutritious food, reliable transportation, and childcare—while having a modest financial cushion for unexpected emergencies and the ability to save toward retirement or a child's future, without living paycheck to paycheck or enjoying vast generational wealth.

### Income Ranges (Pew Research Benchmark)
Sociologists and economists (most notably Pew Research Center) conventionally define middle-income households as those earning between **two-thirds and double the national median income**, adjusted for household size:
* **Lower Class / Lower Income:** Earning less than **$56,600 – $61,000** annually (for a standard 3-person household).
* **Middle Class / Middle Income:** Earning between **$56,600 and $169,800** (roughly $60,000 to $180,000+ depending on current inflation-adjusted benchmark datasets).
* **Upper Class / Upper Income:** Earning more than **$169,800 – $183,000+** annually.

### Factors Beyond Income
1. **Liquid Assets & Net Worth:** Having a 3- to 6-month emergency reserve vs. relying on high-interest debt when unexpected expenses arise.
2. **Homeownership & Equity:** Primary residence ownership remains the single largest driver of American middle-class wealth accumulation.
3. **Job Quality & Non-Wage Benefits:** Employer-sponsored health insurance, paid family leave, and 401(k) matching.
4. **Education Level:** Attainment of a bachelor’s degree or professional trade credential correlates heavily with class mobility and job resilience.
5. **Debt-to-Income Ratio:** Severe student loan debt, medical bills, or vehicle financing can make someone with a high nominal salary live with lower-class financial stress.

---

## 4. Colorado-Specific Class Breakdown & Donor Context

### Income Ranges in Colorado
Colorado has one of the highest median household incomes in the United States (statewide median is approximately **$97,113**, compared to the national median of ~$75,000–$80,000):
* **Lower Class / Lower Income:** Households earning under **$64,742** annually.
* **Middle Class Range:** Households earning between **$64,742 and $194,226** annually (two-thirds to double the state median).
* **Upper-Middle Class:** Starts around **$151,065**.
* **Upper Class / Upper Income:** Households earning above **$194,226** annually.

### Colorado-Specific Factors Beyond Income
1. **Housing Affordability Crunch:** The Front Range (Denver, Boulder, Fort Collins) and mountain communities have extremely high median home values ($550,000 to $650,000+). Because housing absorbs 35%–50% of monthly budgets, a household earning $100,000–$120,000 often feels squeezed and cannot easily buy a home.
2. **Childcare & Early Education Costs:** Colorado consistently ranks among the top five most expensive states for infant and toddler childcare, often costing $18,000 to $24,000 per year per child.
3. **Transportation & Regional Disparity:** Costs along the I-25 corridor and mountain valleys require substantial vehicle and commuting expenditures.

### Donor Messaging Implications
* **Acknowledge the Cost of Living:** Prospective donors in Colorado who earn between $100,000 and $160,000 statistically fall into the middle-to-upper-middle tier, but many feel "house-poor" or financially pressured. Messaging should avoid assuming they "have money to burn."
* **Tangible, Grounded Impact Tiers:** Instead of asking for vague large gifts, frame giving in concrete child-level solutions (e.g., "$50 provides a warm winter coat and winter boots; $150 provides a full semester of school supplies and books").
* **Community-Led Framing:** Donors respond strongly to the idea of protecting local Colorado children who are falling through the cracks of the state’s rapid economic growth.

---
